notes:
Summary: Customer evaluating Redwood Dedicated for production personalization ranking and real-time chat assistant. Primary asks: firm latency SLO definitions across streaming and non-streaming APIs, agreed measurement methodology (client vs server timing), and reserved-GPU planning with throughput guarantees. Key constraints: must run in VPC, strict audit logs, KMS-managed keys, EU data residency for subset of traffic.

SLO alignment discussion (11/20 call):
- Customer insists on p50/p95/p99 split for both endpoint types (batch text generation and streaming chat). Wants p95 <= 120ms for non-streamed reranking calls (short inputs), p95 <= 200ms for streaming initial response, and p99 guards to avoid >500ms spikes.
- We clarified differences: client-side end-to-end (browser SDK + network) vs server-side model-serving latency. Recommended canonical measurement: server ingress-to-last-token-emitted for server SLO; customer to track client-side and map deltas for network.
- Proposed instrumentation: add X-Request-Start header propagation; Redwood will provide per-request server timestamps (ingress, model-start, token-stream-first, token-stream-last). Use histograms (not simple metric averages) and maintain rolling 72h windows.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: we recommended separate SLOs and dashboards. For streaming, primary SLO tied to time-to-first-token (TTFT) and p95 for initial chunk; overall tail tracked by p99 of per-chunk latency. For non-streaming (sync generation / reranking) use end-to-end server latency.

Throughput / reserved capacity planning:
- Customer peak profile: 18k qps short rerank (2-4 tokens), sustained chat bursts 1.2k concurrent streams with average 60 token responses.
- Redwood preliminary sizing: reserved-8 (8 x A100-class) cluster with auto-burst to reserved-12 on major sale events, expected steady throughput 12k qps for rerank and 1.0k concurrent streaming sessions at target SLOs (with batching & KV cache). Detailed sizing spreadsheet shared in drive.
- Load tests planned: staged synthetic replay of production traces (11/30–12/03). Tests to record p50/p95/p99, percent of requests served from cache, batching efficiency, and GPU utilization per-slot.

SLA / commercial notes:
- Customer wants explicit latency credits for p95 breaches (monthly). Legal asked for objective measurement points (server ingress) and a defined measurement window. Redwood proposed standard credit tiers but legal wants sample clause for sustained peak events (black-swan fair-use carveout).
- Negotiation items: definition of "unavailable" vs "degraded latency", burst credit policy, minimum reserved term (12 months vs 24 months).

Risks & open items:
- Measurement alignment: customer engineers prefer client-side SLO; Redwood needs server-side canonical to operate capacity/fallbacks. Need a short tech note that maps server timestamps to observed client deltas.
- Peak burst handling: customer requires firm guarantees for Black Friday-style peaks (2x sustained qps for 6 hours). Need confirmation if reserved with burst can be contractually guaranteed.
- Security questionnaire items outstanding (data residency validation, key rotation process).

Action items (owner in parens):
- Run 72-hour mixed workload test and produce SLO histograms (Ethan).
- Draft "SLO measurement mapping" tech note showing how client times map to server timestamps + recommended SDK header (Sofia).
- Legal/Commercial: circulate SLA term sheet with latency credit table and burst carveouts (AE/Commercial).
- Customer: provide 7 days of production traces (anonymized) for replay and modeling (Granite infra).

Recent timeline (bulleted):
- 2025-11-05: Intro call, product overview, initial requirements capture.
- 2025-11-12: Deep dive on workload profile (Granite infra team).
- 2025-11-20: SLO alignment workshop (Fireflies ff_20251120_Granite_SLOs).
- 2025-11-27: Follow-up on streaming measurement and proposed dashboard metrics (Fireflies ff_20251127_latency_alignment).
- 2025-11-30: Load-test plan finalized; test window 11/30–12/03.

Customer quotes / color: "We need guarantees on tail latency — if p99 jumps, our UX collapses. We can tolerate small p50 variance but not p99 spikes." — lead infra.

Next steps (short): get production traces -> run replay -> provide 72h histogram report -> finalize SLA latency credit language.
